title: Explicit scale degrees
html: The lowercase suffix d keeps an integer a scale degree even inside arithmetic and function calls. By contrast, 3/1 is a ratio. Here sqrt(2d) halves the tuned interval of degree 2, giving degree 1 in 12edo. Try changing the scale to 19edo.

title: Pitch and ratio conversions
html: pitch(...) converts a ratio to an additive pitch interval; ratio(...) converts a pitch interval back to a ratio. Bare integers follow the parameter's meaning: pitch(2) is an octave, while ratio(2) uses scale degree 2. Use d or /1 when you want to make that choice explicit.

title: Measure rests
html: A semicolon outside a tuning block rests until the next measure boundary. At a boundary it rests for a whole measure. Snippets have no default time signature: write @time(...) to use measure rests or validate barlines. Without a meter, ; warns and adds no duration. Change 3/4 to 5/4 to hear the pauses grow.

title: Hold to the end of a group
html: Append ! to hold each attack until its enclosing construction ends. The starting times stay the same, so an arpeggio accumulates into a chord. Operators apply in order: compare (0 4 7)!, (0 4 7)!=, and [0 4 7]!.

props.editorLabel: Hold to the end of a group source

title: Chained glissando
html: Successive @gliss directives join several slides into one held note. A leading = can continue it across a barline or newline. A rest ends the connection.

title: Named values
html: let evaluates an expression once and gives it a name. Declarations consume no beats. Choose names that are not pitch spellings: fifth works, while G already means a note.

props.source:
let fifth = 3/2
let third = 5/4
1/1 third fifth
[1/1, third, fifth]===

title: Functions and defaults
html: Define a function with fn and return its result with ret. Parameters can have trailing defaults. An unannotated pitch argument follows the caller's scale. Functions cannot call themselves recursively; use repeats for repetition.

props.source:
fn transpose(note, interval = 3/2) { ret note + interval }
C transpose(C)
D transpose(D, 5/4)
{19edo} 0 transpose(0)

title: Returning musical phrases
description: A function can return a whole musical fragment, including rhythm and directives. Each call inherits the current tuning and timing context. Change the phrase once to update both calls.

title: Local bindings and closures
description: A function captures the named bindings visible when it is defined. Later declarations can shadow those names. Groups and parallel branches keep their own local declarations.

props.source:
let interval = 3/2
fn remembered() { ret interval }
(let interval = 5/4
 interval remembered())
interval remembered()

title: Parameter coercions
html: Annotations specify how arguments are interpreted: ratio, pitch, integer, boolean, or container. Coercions can nest, as in container<ratio>. A bare integer in a ratio argument is a scalar; an explicit d degree supplies its tuned ratio.

title: Container indexing
html: Square brackets can hold values for later use in expressions. Index from zero with values[0]; negative indices count from the end. Nested containers support repeated indexing. A bracketed score written directly in the music still follows the usual chord or tuplet rules.

props.source:
let pitches = [1/1, 5/4, 3/2, 2/1]
pitches[0] pitches[1] pitches[-1] pitches[2]
let nested = [[1/1, 5/4], [3/2, 2/1]]
nested[1][0]

title: Optional values
html: niente represents a missing value. Use al to choose a fallback only when the left side is missing. It is useful for optional function parameters.

props.source:
fn choose(note = niente) { ret note al 1/1 }
choose() choose(5/4) choose(3/2) choose(niente)

title: Conditional expressions
html: value if condition else other evaluates only the selected branch. Try changing the boolean argument to switch the chord's third.

title: Scales from expressions
html: {scale = expression} builds a scale from a container or function result. Entries become degrees 1 onward; degree 0 remains the root, and the final entry sets the equave. Arithmetic can shift every member of the returned container.

title: Sorting scale entries
description: sort() puts numeric container values in ascending order. Use it when a generated scale would otherwise put its degrees out of order.

title: Mapping with lambdas
html: A lambda such as (value) => value + 100c is an inline function. arrayMap(callback, values) applies it to each member of a container.

title: Reducing a container
html: arrayReduce(callback, values, initial) combines a container into one result. The callback receives the accumulated result and the next element. Here three pure fifths combine into 27/8.

props.source:
let stack = arrayReduce((total, interval) => total * interval, [3/2, 3/2, 3/2], 1/1)
1/1 3/2 9/4 stack

title: Products and combinations
html: prod(values) multiplies interval ratios. kCombinations(values, count) lists all subsets of the requested size. Combining them produces the pairwise products 15, 21, and 35 from factors 3, 5, and 7.

title: Grounding a scale
html: ground(values) shifts the first entry to unison and moves the others by the same interval. Here 3:5:7 becomes 1/1, 5/3, and 7/3.

title: Equave reduction
html: equaveReduce(values, equave) moves ratios into one equave; the rd operator performs the reduction directly. If the second argument is omitted, the last container entry supplies the equave. Reducing 3/1, 5/1, and 7/1 by 2/1 gives 3/2, 5/4, and 7/4.

title: Combination product sets
html: cps(factors, count) combines products, grounding, equave reduction, and sorting into a scale helper. Optional arguments set the equave and whether to retain the products' original unity. Try replacing 7 with 11 or changing the combination size.

title: Combined tuning assignments
html: Separate tuning assignments inside braces with semicolons. This lets you construct a scale and choose its mode in one block. A semicolon inside braces separates assignments; outside braces it is a measure rest.

title: Tempo changes in snippets
html: @tempo(...bpm) changes playback speed without changing beat durations. Snippets support tempo changes inside the score; in the DAW, put tempo directives in the global source. Change 120bpm below and compare the two phrases.

title: Note envelopes
html: @adsr(attack, decay, sustain, release) controls each note's loudness envelope. Times use ms or s, and sustain is a level such as 60%. Try lengthening the attack or release.

title: Unison voices and spread
html: The unison instrument layers detuned voices. This example uses five voices and @spread(20c) in its lane settings. Change the voice count or waveform below to compare the sound. In the DAW, set @spread(...c) in the instrument lane source; it does not control spread from a clip.

title: Continuous signal ramps
html:
@ramp connects the next two occurrences of the same signal directive over the intervening beats. It supports the same easing curves as @gliss. This unison lane widens from 0c to 40c over eight beats, then narrows to 5c over four beats. Its lane source is:

@ramp(ease-in-out) @spread(0c) ........
@ramp @spread(40c) ....
@spread(5c)

Edit the held notes below to hear the same automation with a different chord.

title: Delay effect lanes
html:
In the DAW, add a ping-pong delay effect lane and route an instrument to it in the mixer. Its source supports @delay(250ms), @feedback(55%), @wet(35%), and @separation(100%). Separation controls the stereo width. These directives belong to the effect lane, not a note snippet.

All four parameters support @ramp. For example, this effect source raises the wet level over eight beats:

@delay(250ms) @feedback(55%) @separation(100%)
@ramp(ease-in) @wet(10%) ........ @wet(60%)
